record.original_question: When n = 10 straight lines are used in the Kobon triangle problem, is the best known upper bound non-sharp, or does there exist a configuration of 10 lines in the plane that forms 26 nonoverlapping, uncut triangles?

evidence.quote: Particular case of Problem 1. The best configuration known with 10 lines has 25 triangles. But the bound by Clement and Bader only guarantees that K(10) ≤ 26. Maybe the bound is not tight enough? or it is possible to find a configuration with 10 lines and 26 triangles?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider arrangements of n straight lines in the Euclidean plane, in general position in the sense that no two lines are parallel and no three are concurrent. Such an arrangement partitions the plane into open regions; among these are triangular regions, i.e., bounded regions whose closure is a triangle. A triangle in the arrangement is called "uncut" if no line of the arrangement passes through its interior (equivalently, each of its three sides is a full segment between two consecutive intersection points along its supporting line), and a collection of such triangles is called "nonoverlapping" if their interiors are pairwise disjoint. Let K(n) denote the maximum number of nonoverlapping uncut triangles that can be formed by an arrangement of n lines in the plane.

It is known that K(10) ≤ 26 (the Clément–Bader upper bound) and that there exists an arrangement of 10 lines realizing 25 nonoverlapping uncut triangles.

Determine K(10): does there exist an arrangement of 10 lines in the plane forming 26 nonoverlapping uncut triangles, or is the true maximum equal to 25 (so that the upper bound 26 is not tight)?
artifact.status_search_result: The Kobon triangle problem for n = 10 remains open. The best known lower bound is 25 (achieved by configurations going back to Grünbaum 1967), while the best known upper bound is 26 (Clément–Bader). It is not known whether a 10-line arrangement attaining 26 nonoverlapping uncut triangles exists, nor whether the upper bound can be improved to 25. Recent computational work (e.g., SAT-based searches in 2025) has not resolved this case.

status_evidence.claim: K(10) is between 25 and 26 with the exact value unresolved.
